Habilitation
The habilitation process gives qualified young scientists the opportunity to qualify for a professorship and to independently perform research and teaching tasks for this purpose. More detailed information is available from the departments.
Â© Eugen Gebhardt
Habilitation procedure
I. Application for teaching qualification
Submission of application to the dean's office
Approval by the faculty council and subsequent announcement
Agreement on objectives between candidate and subject mentors (PDF to the dean's office)
After approx. 2 years: Interim evaluation (PDF to the Dean's Office)
After approx. 4 years: Submission of habilitation thesis to the Dean's Office
Obtaining expert opinions; approval by the faculty council
Scientific discussion
Preparation of laudatio by subject mentors, approval by the faculty council
II. Application for teaching authorization
After receiving the teaching qualification certificate, an application for teaching authorization can be submitted, which entitles the holder to use the title PD.
The following must be submitted:
Personnel questionnaire (Dean's Office)
Declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Dean's Office)
Curriculum vitae
Certificates of (1) university degree, (2) doctorate, (3) teaching qualification
Proof of current full-time employment
Documents for the application
Habilitation regulations (PDF, 50 KB)
Checklist (PDF, 141 KB)
Declaration habilitation attempt (PDF, 73 KB)
Declaration research allowance (PDF, 51 KB)
Chairs and Work Groups
Documents for the submission of your thesis
Checklist thesis submission (PDF, 145 KB)
Declaration habilitation procedures (PDF, 71 KB)
Declaration of academic integrity (PDF, 54 KB)
